from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "A matrix is a mathematical function mapping spaces.",
            "Square matrices map a space into itself.",
            "Non-square matrices bridge spaces of different dimensions."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Refresher: The Mapping Concept", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        v = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP*1.5, color=BLUE)
        v_label = MathTex("\\vec{v}", color=BLUE).next_to(v, RIGHT)
        T_label = MathTex("T", color=YELLOW).next_to(v, LEFT)
        transformed_v = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5 + UP*0.5, color=GREEN)
        transformed_v_label = MathTex("T(\\vec{v})", color=GREEN).next_to(transformed_v, RIGHT)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Create(v), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(T_label))
        self.play(v.animate.rotate(PI/4), v_label.animate.rotate(PI/4))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(FadeOut(v), FadeOut(v_label), FadeOut(T_label))
        self.play(Create(transformed_v), Write(transformed_v_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Tall matrices have more rows than columns.",
            "They embed lower dimensions into higher ones.",
            "Think of a 2D plane in 3D.",
            "A simple stick figure in 3D space.",
            "Represented by a 3x2 matrix transformation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Case 1: Dimensional Expansion (Tall Matrices)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Matrix visualization
        matrix = MathTex(r"\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \\ e & f \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \\ z' \end{pmatrix}")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Setup 3D space for subspace visualization
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        axes.set_color(GRAY)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'E3', scale_factor=0.4)
        
        # Grid manifold (embedded)
        grid_plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-1, 1], y_range=[-1, 1], background_line_style={"stroke_color": BLUE, "stroke_opacity": 0.5})
        self.place_at_grid(grid_plane, 'E3', scale_factor=0.2)
        grid_plane.rotate(PI/4, axis=RIGHT)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Write(matrix))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(axes))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(grid_plane))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Simple stick figure as line
        stick_fig = VGroup(Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5), Line(DOWN*0.5, DOWN*0.8+LEFT*0.3), Line(DOWN*0.5, DOWN*0.8+RIGHT*0.3)).set_color(RED)
        self.place_at_grid(stick_fig, 'E3', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(stick_fig))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(matrix.animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Dimensional Compression (Wide Matrices)", [
            "Wide matrices have more columns than rows.",
            "They compress higher dimensions into lower ones.",
            "This process is called linear projection.",
            "Like a camera flattening 3D to 2D.",
            "Information is lost during this compression."
        ])
        
        # Create visual elements
        matrix = MathTex(r"\begin{bmatrix} a & b & c \\ d & e & f \end{bmatrix}", color=BLUE)
        space_n = Text("R^3 (Input Space)", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        space_m = Text("R^2 (Output Space)", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
        vector_v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*0.5+UP*0.5, color=WHITE)
        projection_line = Line(start=np.array([0,0,0]), end=np.array([0,0,1]), color=RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(space_n, 'A4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(space_m, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(space_n), FadeIn(space_m))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.place_at_grid(vector_v, 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(vector_v))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_at_grid(projection_line, 'C4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(projection_line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        self.play(FadeOut(projection_line), FadeOut(vector_v))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visual Synthesis & Summary", [
            "Tall matrices unfold or embed objects.",
            "Wide matrices flatten or project objects.",
            "Transformation is simply mapping between spaces."
        ])
        
        # Create objects for tall transformation (2D -> 3D)
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color=BLUE)
        cube = Cube(side_length=1.0, fill_opacity=0.3, color=BLUE)
        
        # Create objects for wide transformation (3D -> 2D)
        cube_wide = Cube(side_length=1.0, fill_opacity=0.3, color=YELLOW)
        square_wide = Square(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.3, color=YELLOW)
        
        # Group them
        tall_group = VGroup(square, cube)
        wide_group = VGroup(cube_wide, square_wide)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(square, "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(square))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(square, cube))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(cube_wide, "B5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(cube_wide))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(cube_wide, square_wide))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        combined = VGroup(cube, square_wide)
        self.play(combined.animate.set_opacity(0.8))
        self.play(Flash(combined))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Geometric Interpretation of Non-Square Matrices as Dimensional Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Mapping Concept
sections.content: Define a matrix as a function (transformation). A square matrix (n x n) maps a space to itself, but non-square matrices (m x n) represent a bridge between spaces of different dimensions (e.g., R^n to R^m).
sections.example: Visualizing a 2D plane (flat sheet) and a 3D space (room). A matrix acts as the 'instructions' to move from one to the other.

sections.title: Case 1: Dimensional Expansion (Tall Matrices)
sections.content: Explain m > n matrices. These embed lower-dimensional objects into higher-dimensional spaces. The transformation creates a 'subspace' within the larger target dimension.
sections.example: A 2D 'stick-figure' character drawn on a flat screen (R^2) being projected into a 3D hologram (R^3) using a 3x2 matrix.

sections.title: Case 2: Dimensional Compression (Wide Matrices)
sections.content: Explain n > m matrices. These collapse higher-dimensional information into a lower dimension. Emphasize the concept of 'Projection' and the loss of information (Kernel/Null space).
sections.example: A 3D robotic arm's position (x, y, z) being tracked by a 2D security camera sensor (u, v) using a 2x3 matrix, essentially 'flattening' the 3D movement onto a 2D image plane.

sections.title: Visual Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Synthesize the two cases: Transformation = Mapping. Tall matrices 'unfold' or 'embed'; Wide matrices 'flatten' or 'project'.
sections.example: Show an animation of a 3D cube collapsing into a 2D shadow (wide matrix) and a 2D drawing expanding into a 3D wireframe model (tall matrix) simultaneously on screen.
